questions.q: What does the do-less-then-obsess principle ask you to do?
a: Choose few activities, then commit intense effort to them
Work fewer hours but hide it from your boss
Delegate most tasks and focus on networking
Say no to every request without exception
questions.why: Lesson 1 says top performers select a few activities and then apply intense, targeted effort.

questions.q: What surprising finding does Hansen report about collaboration?
a: Top performers collaborate less than average workers
Top performers collaborate more than anyone
Collaboration matters only in creative fields
Remote teams collaborate better than in-person ones
questions.why: Lesson 3 says top performers work together only when it clearly adds value.

Prioritizing projects and planning them carefully
Practicing persistently until skills become automatic
Pairing performance goals with public praise
questions.why: Lesson 2 says passion alone is not enough; top performers match it with purpose.

questions.q: How does the learning loop work?
a: Ask for feedback regularly and use it to refine your process
Study a skill for 10,000 hours before using it
Repeat the same tasks until they feel easy
Learn from books rather than from colleagues
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends regular feedback instead of mindless repetition to keep improving.

questions.q: What does the fight-and-unite meeting method involve?
a: Debate openly first, then commit to the leader's decision
Vote on every idea until everyone agrees
Keep discussion brief and avoid disagreement
Let the most senior person speak last
questions.why: Lesson 3 says teams should debate diverse views, then unite behind the final choice.
